properties.NAME: Biscayne Bay
properties.PRESERVE_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY:
Established in 1975, the Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve is the larger of the two Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserves, at 64,607 acres. Along with the Biscayne Bay-Cape Florida to Monroe County Line Aquatic Preserve, the two are collectively known as the Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserves (BBAP). Together, these two preserves cover over 68,000 acres and are divided by 172,000 acres of the Biscayne National Park in the central section of Biscayne Bay. 
Marine communities represent the majority of the area within the preserve and include seagrass beds, algal beds, and a limited shoreline of salt marsh and mangrove swamp. These areas provide habitat for a variety of species including several of concern such as the Florida manatee, smalltooth sawfish, and the American crocodile. Known as a premier fishing and scuba diving destination, visitors to the preserve can engage in a variety of recreational activities. Popular pursuits include power boating, sail boating, canoeing, water skiing, hang gliding, swimming, windsurfing, and of course, snorkeling, scuba diving, and fishing, all which provide excellent opportunities to explore and enjoy the preserve's rich aquatic environment.
properties.SHORT_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY: Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve extends the length of Biscayne Bay from the headwaters of the Oleta River south to Card Sound near Key Largo. It excludes all waters of Biscayne National Park and lies east of Miami Dade County.

properties.NAME: Biscayne Bay-Cape Florida to Monroe County Line
properties.PRESERVE_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY:
The Biscayne Bay-Cape Florida to Monroe County Line Aquatic Preserve, established in 1975, covers 4,163 acres off the eastern shore of Key Biscayne. Originally larger, the preserve lost much of its original acreage when Biscayne National Monument was designated a National Park in 1980. Today, much of the submerged lands and islands originally included within its boundaries are now within either Biscayne National Park or within the larger of the two Biscayne Bay aquatic preserves, Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve. Much of the area of the Biscayne Bay-Cape Florida to Monroe County Line Aquatic Preserve is entirely submerged and includes about one mile of Cape Florida's shoreline within its boundaries. 
The preserve is home to several natural communities such as seagrass and algal beds, which serve as crucial habitats and food sources for a diversity of marine life. Visitors to the preserve enjoy a variety of recreational activities, including boating, swimming, fishing, and snorkeling, allowing them to explore and enjoy the preserve's rich aquatic environment.
properties.SHORT_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY: Cape Florida Aquatic Preserve sits off the eastern coast of Key Biscayne, extending roughly 3 miles into the Atlantic Ocean.
